e: name:'Gulf LNG'
v: Gulf LNG

e: note:'Qatar accounts for ~75% of Gulf LNG. Total annual flow: $51.5B. All cargo must transit Hormuz - no alternative maritime route exists.'
v: Qatar accounts for ~75% of Gulf LNG. Total annual flow: $51.5B. All cargo must transit Hormuz - no alternative maritime route exists.

e: name:'Hormuz'
v: Hormuz

e: note:'Single mandatory transit for 100% of Gulf LNG. The full width of this node represents the entire $51.5B annual exposure at one bottleneck.'
v: Single mandatory transit for 100% of Gulf LNG. The full width of this node represents the entire $51.5B annual exposure at one bottleneck.

e: name:'Malacca'
v: Malacca

e: note:'Second mandatory chokepoint for all Asia-Pacific LNG. $27.8B - 54% of Gulf LNG - passes here. No viable bypass exists for laden tankers.'
v: Second mandatory chokepoint for all Asia-Pacific LNG. $27.8B - 54% of Gulf LNG - passes here. No viable bypass exists for laden tankers.

e: name:'Bab el-Mandeb / Suez'
v: Bab el-Mandeb / Suez

e: note:'Bab el-Mandeb (active Houthi threat zone since late 2023) and Suez Canal in sequence. $19.1B - 37% of Gulf LNG. Disruption adds 14-16 days around the Cape.'
v: Bab el-Mandeb (active Houthi threat zone since late 2023) and Suez Canal in sequence. $19.1B - 37% of Gulf LNG. Disruption adds 14-16 days around the Cape.

e: name:'Gibraltar'
v: Gibraltar

e: note:'Transit point for Atlantic-facing European terminals. Belgium (Zeebrugge), UK (Isle of Grain, South Hook) and Netherlands (Gate Rotterdam) all transit Gibraltar. France, Italy and Spain use Mediterranean terminals and bypass it.'
v: Transit point for Atlantic-facing European terminals. Belgium (Zeebrugge), UK (Isle of Grain, South Hook) and Netherlands (Gate Rotterdam) all transit Gibraltar. France, Italy and Spain use Mediterranean terminals and bypass it.

e: name:'China'
v: China

e: note:'Largest single buyer of Gulf LNG. 23.6% of Chinese imports via Hormuz and Malacca.'
v: Largest single buyer of Gulf LNG. 23.6% of Chinese imports via Hormuz and Malacca.

v: S. Korea

e: note:'20.0% of South Korean LNG via Hormuz. Route continues through the Taiwan and Korea Straits.'

v: Japan

e: note:'6.5% of Japanese imports via Hormuz. Japan has diversified substantially to Australian and US LNG.'
